signals.entity: All Bulgarian traders, plus banks' tariff/price disclosures, ATM screens/receipts and POS terminal receipts
signals.signal: [LIVE DEADLINE] Bulgaria's DUAL PRICE DISPLAY (prices shown simultaneously in euro AND lev) ENDS 08/08/2026. Re-verified in the consolidated statute: Law on the Introduction of the Euro in the Republic of Bulgaria (ZVERB) Art.15(2), as amended by Darjaven Vestnik No.65/2025 — 'Периодът на двойно обозначаване на цените на стоките и услугите в евро и в левове започва на 8 август 2025 г. и приключва на 8 август 2026 г.' [The dual-display period begins 8 August 2025 and ends 8 August 2026]. Independently restated by the BNB's own euro-changeover Q&A page on dual price display (regulator source) and by KZP (Komisiya za zashtita na potrebitelite — Consumer Protection Commission) news item No.389 of 29/01/2026. No extension is proposed; the period was in fact SHORTENED during drafting (from end-2026 to 08/08/2026). Sanctions re-read line by line in ZVERB Art.59 and all match: breach of Art.15(1) — individuals BGN 400–5,000 (repeat BGN 800–10,000), legal persons/sole traders BGN 600–7,000 (repeat BGN 1,200–14,000); breach of Art.15(4) (the fair-and-transparent pricing duty, which obliges traders to justify any price increase by objective economic factors on request) — individuals BGN 1,000–10,000 (repeat BGN 2,000–20,000), legal persons BGN 5,000–100,000 (repeat BGN 10,000–200,000); Art.59(6) — for an undertaking with prior-financial-year turnover above BGN 50,000,000, up to 0.5% of that turnover, rising to 1% for a repeat of the same breach WITHIN the dual-display period, capped at BGN 1,000,000. ADVERSARIAL CORRECTION on enforcement: the researcher named only KZP and the NRA. ZVERB Art.60(1) in fact designates FIVE issuing authorities, and for a BANK the acts are drawn up by officials authorised by the relevant BNB Deputy Governor (Art.60(1)(1)), not by KZP — KZP polices merchants, BNB polices its supervised entities. That materially changes who a bank's compliance owner talks to.
signals.source_name: lex.bg — ZVERB consolidated text, Art.15, Art.59, Art.60 (re-fetched with desktop UA after 403); corroborated by BNB euro Q&A 'Двойно обозначаване на цените в евро и левове' and KZP news item 29/01/2026
signals.implies: (a) WHO: every Bulgarian bank (branch tariffs, statements, ATM on-screen text and receipts, POS/e-commerce receipts) and every card-accepting merchant on a Printec-managed POS estate. (b) WHAT: a content/software release across the estate — POS terminal application plus TMS (Terminal Management System) push to drop the lev leg from receipts and prompts; ATM screen and receipt template changes through NCR x-core multivendor software; document-management updates to tariffs and pre-contractual information. (c) WHEN: budget is already committed — this is an execution week. The sellable item is the change-release, regression test and rollback plan as a managed service, plus a post-09/08/2026 audit that no lev leg was left behind on any device.
signals.likelihood: Certain — statutory date, 6 days after this run; no extension proposed
signals.followup: Confirm with Bulgarian bank and retail clients whether dual display is switched off exactly on 08/08/2026 or kept voluntarily. Voluntary continuation is permitted, but the turnover-based sanctions in Art.59(6) are tied to a repeat 'within the dual-display period', so the exposure profile changes on 09/08/2026 — this is a contested-interpretation point and must be referred to Printec Compliance/DPO, not answered by the research team. For bank clients, route the compliance conversation via BNB (Art.60(1)(1)), not KZP.
signals.verifier_note: CONFIRMED against two primary sources re-read this run. lex.bg returned 403 to the standard fetcher; re-fetched successfully with a desktop User-Agent (HTTP 200, 570KB) and text-extracted locally — Art.15(2), Art.59(1)(2), Art.59(1)(6), Art.59(4)(2), Art.59(4)(6), Art.59(5)(2), Art.59(5)(6), Art.59(6) all match the researcher's figures exactly. BNB's own Q&A page independently states 'на 8 август 2025 г. и ще приключи на 8 август 2026 г.' Two corrections: (i) the researcher attributed the turnover sanction to 'Art.59(6)-(7)' — Art.59(7) is a DIFFERENT and harsher band (up to 1% of turnover, 2% on repeat, same BGN 1m cap) applying to non-compliance with enforcement measures under Art.57(5), not to Art.15(4); (ii) enforcement is not KZP+NRA only — Art.60(1) lists BNB Deputy Governor (for BNB-supervised entities, i.e. banks), FSC Deputy Chair, NRA Executive Director, the Minister of Innovation and Digital Transformation and the KZP Chair. Also corrected source_date: the researcher had put the future deadline (08/08/2026) in the source-date field; the most recent dated triggering source is the KZP guidance of 29/01/2026. is_new set to false — the date has been statutory since DV 65/2025 and predates the 24/07/2026 baseline.

signals.entity: All Bulgarian credit institutions (UniCredit Bulbank, DSK, UBB, Postbank, Fibank, ProCredit, Allianz Bank etc.) and Bulgarian Posts EAD
signals.signal: Residual lev-exchange calendar, re-read directly in ZVERB Art.26. (1) BNB exchanges lev banknotes AND coins into euro free of charge, in unlimited quantity and WITHOUT ANY TIME LIMIT, at the official rate (1.95583 BGN/EUR). (2) Credit institutions had to exchange free of charge and in unlimited quantity for the FIRST 6 MONTHS from euro introduction (01/01/2026–30/06/2026), with a 3-working-day advance order required for a single transaction above BGN 30,000; the same applies to depositing lev cash into a euro account at the exchanging bank. (3)–(5) Bulgarian Posts EAD served only settlements with no bank office or branch, as a Service of General Economic Interest for 6 months, free, up to BGN 1,000/day per person, BGN 1,000–10,000/day only on 3–5 working days' advance order at pre-announced branches, and nothing above BGN 10,000/day. (6)–(7) After those periods banks and Bulgarian Posts MAY introduce a fee. (8) Until 12 months from euro introduction — i.e. through 31/12/2026 — credit institutions MAY NOT REFUSE the Art.26(2) service (Bulgarian Posts may refuse only for lack of cash). (9) Only AFTER those 12 months, i.e. from 01/01/2027, may banks and Bulgarian Posts DISCONTINUE cash lev–euro exchange. Failure to comply with Art.26(2), (6), (8), (9)–(10) or (12) carries a property sanction of BGN 5,000–30,000, doubling to BGN 10,000–60,000 on repeat (Art.59(5)(11)). BNB press release of 01/07/2026, re-fetched and confirmed verbatim: as at 30/06/2026, 29.4 billion leva had been exchanged, '94.48% от левовите банкноти и разменни монети' in circulation; approximately 1.7 billion leva in notes and coins remain outside BNB vaults; euro net issuance in Bulgaria stood at EUR 8.8 billion; from 01/07/2026 banks may charge a fee but must notify BNB, while BNB itself continues unlimited free exchange indefinitely.
signals.source_name: BNB press release 01/07/2026 (Bulgarian) + lex.bg ZVERB Art.26 and Art.59(5)(11) (re-fetched with desktop UA)
signals.implies: (a) WHO: every Bulgarian bank branch network — all still carry a NON-REFUSABLE manual lev-exchange duty until 31/12/2026, then face a discretionary wind-down decision, with BGN 1.7bn of lev still outstanding and BNB's own counters obliged to absorb it indefinitely. (b) WHAT: teller cash recyclers (Glory / Sesami TCR) and branch cash automation to keep serving residual exchange at near-zero teller cost; NCR intelligent-deposit / recycling ATMs to absorb residual euro cash-in; NCR APTRA OptiCash re-forecasting because branch cash mix, vault holdings and CIT frequency all shift once lev exchange stops; Printec managed/field services for vault and device changes. (c) WHEN: budget must commit in Q3–Q4 2026 for anything to be in place at the 01/01/2027 decision point.
signals.likelihood: High — statutory; every bank must take a documented, pre-notified decision before 01/01/2027
signals.followup: Ask each Bulgarian bank client whether it will discontinue lev exchange from 01/01/2027 — it must pre-notify BNB under Ordinance No.47 Art.2(4) (re-verified this run) — and use that decision as the entry point for a branch cash-automation / recycler consolidation proposal. Separately, obtain each client's Art.26(6) fee notification to size residual counter volumes.
signals.verifier_note: CONFIRMED. ZVERB Art.26(1)-(10) re-read in the consolidated Bulgarian text — every sub-paragraph the researcher cited is accurate, including the BGN 30,000 / 3-working-day threshold, the BGN 1,000 and BGN 1,000–10,000 / 3–5-working-day Bulgarian Posts limits and the 6/12-month gates. BNB press release re-fetched: 29.4bn leva, 94.48%, 1.7bn leva outstanding and EUR 8.8bn net issuance all match exactly. TWO CLAIMS NOT CONFIRMED and downgraded in the text above: (i) the direct quote attributed to BNB that it 'has no authority to intervene in these decisions' did not appear in the re-fetched release (the release states banks may charge and must notify BNB) — quote removed, substance retained; (ii) 'Bulgarian Posts introduced its fee from 29/06/2026' could not be independently verified against a Bulgarian Posts or BNB source this run — claim dropped rather than repeated. Added the Art.59(5)(11) sanction band, which the researcher omitted and which is the actual enforcement lever on banks. is_new set to false: the release predates the 24/07/2026 baseline.

signals.entity: Bulgarian banks, their cash-in-transit / cash-handling service providers, financial institutions and bureaux de change
signals.signal: [STANDING — dated 31/07/2025; in force 01/01/2026] BNB Ordinance No.18 of 31 July 2025 on quality control of euro banknotes and coins in cash circulation (Darjaven Vestnik No.68 of 19/08/2025, in force 01/01/2026) applies the Eurosystem recirculation regime in Bulgaria. Re-extracted from the BNB PDF this run. Art.28(1): banks and service providers may process euro banknotes and coins ONLY on machines that have passed manufacturer tests and are on the list published by the ECB (banknotes) or the European Commission (coins). Art.28(2): those machines are subject to BNB control tests. Art.28(3): BNB does NOT test (1) ATM terminal devices or (2) self-service machines that do not identify the user — an important scoping limit. Art.28(4): self-service machines may be loaded only with banknotes checked for authenticity and fitness under ECB Decision 2010/14. Art.29: banks and service providers must train staff on the machines they use, and an untrained employee may not operate a sorting or self-service machine. Art.30–31: a BNB recognition control test passes ONLY at 100% correct identification of the counterfeit test set; a fitness test passes only if at most 5% of the unfit euro banknotes in the test set are categorised as fit. Art.32(1): a listed machine that FAILS a BNB control test is WITHDRAWN FROM OPERATION and placed under observation for one month; (2) within that month the service operator must apply for a re-test, and the machine may be used again only after passing it; (3) if it fails the re-test the procedure is repeated OR the machine is withdrawn from operation. Art.33: BNB also runs control tests on request from manufacturers, banks, service providers and service operators. Art.35: banks, service providers, financial institutions and bureaux de change must adopt internal rules. Art.36: reporting to BNB per Annex IV of ECB/2010/14 and Art.12 of Regulation (EU) No 1210/2010 through the BNB Integrated Information System; notification of any cash-handling outsourcing agreement (conclusion, amendment or termination) within 10 WORKING DAYS; declaration of the anti-theft banknote-staining chemical used, with a sample. Art.37–38: BNB may conduct on-site, documentary AND 'таен клиент' [mystery shopper] inspections, and inspectors may demand records of machines bought/leased, their servicing and their SOFTWARE UPDATES.
signals.source_name: BNB Ordinance No.18 of 31/07/2025 (PDF, Bulgarian) — re-downloaded independently this run (HTTP 200, 223 KB) and text-extracted with pdfminer
signals.implies: (a) WHO: every Bulgarian bank running recyclers, back-office sorters or customer-identifying self-service deposit machines, plus every CIT/cash-handling outsourcer they use. NOTE the Art.28(3) carve-out: plain ATMs and non-identifying self-service machines are NOT BNB-tested, so the test-failure risk concentrates on SORTERS, TCRs and identified-customer recyclers — pitch accordingly rather than to the whole ATM fleet. (b) WHAT: the strongest hardware driver in this workstream — ECB-listed, fitness-capable NCR recyclers and Glory / Sesami TCRs; because a failed BNB control test takes a machine off-line for at least a month, SLA-backed field service (Printec's 500+ engineers), sensor calibration, firmware currency and device telemetry become contractual rather than optional; Art.38(5) explicitly lets BNB inspect software-update records, which is a direct managed-service hook. The Annex IV reporting duty and the 10-working-day outsourcing notification are a data/managed-service sell. Printec, as an outsourced service provider, is itself directly in scope of Art.28-29, Art.35 and Art.36. (c) WHEN: spend is in-year — the ordinance has been in force since 01/01/2026 and control tests run through 2026, so remediation cannot be deferred to a 2027 budget.
signals.likelihood: High — in force and enforceable now
signals.followup: Obtain the BNB Issue Department implementing instructions ('указания') issued under Ordinance No.18 and the control-test schedule/procedure; then audit each Bulgarian client's installed base against the current ECB tested-machines list, separating in-scope sorters/identifying recyclers from out-of-scope ATMs per Art.28(3), and flag any in-scope device not on the list.
signals.verifier_note: CONFIRMED by independent re-download and local text extraction of the BNB PDF (not relying on the researcher's copy). Title, date 31/07/2025, DV No.68 of 19/08/2025 and entry into force 01/01/2026 all appear on the cover page. Art.28(1)-(4), Art.29(1)-(2), Art.31(2) (100% recognition) and Art.31(3) (max 5% unfit categorised as fit), Art.32(1) (withdrawal + one-month observation), Art.35 and Art.36(1)-(4) all verified verbatim. ONE CORRECTION: the researcher wrote 'repeated failure means permanent withdrawal' — Art.32(3) actually says that on failing the re-test 'процедурата по ал. 1 и 2 се повтаря ИЛИ машината се извежда от експлоатация' (the procedure is repeated OR the machine is withdrawn), i.e. permanent withdrawal is one option, not automatic. Also added two material items the researcher missed: the Art.28(3) scoping carve-out for ATMs and non-identifying self-service machines (which narrows the addressable estate and should not be oversold), and Art.37-38 mystery-shopper inspections plus BNB's right to demand software-update records. 'Documented' training is the researcher's gloss — Art.29 requires training and bars untrained operation but does not use the word. is_new=false: ordinance dates from July 2025.

signals.entity: All Bulgarian ATM deployers — banks and independent ATM deployers
signals.signal: [STANDING — dated 31/07/2025] BNB Ordinance No.46 of 31 July 2025 on initial frontloading and sub-frontloading with euro banknotes, euro coins and euro coin starter kits (DV No.68 of 19/08/2025). Re-extracted from the BNB PDF this run. Art.18(1): 'В срок до датата на въвеждане на еврото банките организират зареждането на обслужваните от нея машини за самообслужване' [by the euro introduction date banks shall organise the loading of the self-service machines they service] as follows — ATMs using TWO euro banknote cassettes are loaded with EUR 10 and EUR 20; ATMs using THREE cassettes with EUR 10 and EUR 20, optionally also EUR 5 and/or EUR 50; ATMs using FOUR cassettes with EUR 10 and EUR 20, optionally also EUR 5 and/or EUR 50 and/or EUR 100, where (a) withdrawals of EUR 100 or less must ALWAYS be served from EUR 5, 10, 20 and/or 50 notes and (b) withdrawals above EUR 100 may also use EUR 50 and/or EUR 100. Art.18(2): from the euro introduction date, cash withdrawals from self-service machines including ATMs dispense ONLY euro banknotes (mirrored in ZVERB Art.23(6)). Art.19: banks report frontloading/sub-frontloading data to BNB in the manner set by BNB instructions and must IMMEDIATELY inform BNB of any case — including suspected cases — of euro cash released into circulation before the introduction date, broken down by denomination. Art.20: BNB may carry out on-site inspections of banks, their appointed representatives and sub-frontloaded persons, plus documentary inspections, each closing with a formal 'констативен протокол' signed by both sides. Sanction for breaching ZVERB Art.23(6): BGN 500–3,000 for individuals (Art.59(1)(4)) and a BGN 5,000–30,000 property sanction for legal persons, doubling to BGN 10,000–60,000 on repeat (Art.59(5)(11)) — both re-checked in the statute. IMPORTANT SCOPE CAVEAT ADDED ON VERIFICATION: this is a CHANGEOVER-LOGISTICS ordinance and Art.18(1) is expressed as a duty owed 'by the euro introduction date', so it should be read as the denomination architecture banks had to have in place for the changeover, not as a proven open-ended, permanently enforceable denomination mandate. Nothing in the ordinance text states it lapses either — treat the mix as the de facto operating standard, but do not present it to a client as a standing legal requirement without a BNB confirmation.
signals.source_name: BNB Ordinance No.46 of 31/07/2025 (PDF, Bulgarian) — re-downloaded independently this run (HTTP 200, 112 KB) and text-extracted with pdfminer
signals.implies: (a) WHO: every bank and independent deployer running an ATM in Bulgaria. (b) WHAT: the denomination architecture drives cassette-count decisions — a 2-cassette ATM cannot offer EUR 5, 50 or 100 under this mix, so any bank wanting a low-denomination or high-value proposition needs 3- or 4-cassette NCR hardware or a recycler; NCR APTRA OptiCash forecasting has to be re-parameterised for a constrained denomination MIX, not just volume; NCR x-core multivendor software must enforce the sub-EUR-100 rule in withdrawal menu logic. (c) WHEN: feeds the 2026-2027 ATM refresh cycle — banks are sizing swap-out lists now, in the first full year of euro operation. Sell it as an operating-standard and cash-efficiency argument; do not lead with 'you are non-compliant', because the legal duty is framed against the changeover date.
signals.likelihood: High that the mix is the operating standard; the open-ended legal force of Art.18(1) beyond the changeover date is not established
signals.followup: Run a cassette-count audit of Bulgarian clients' installed base and produce the list of 2-cassette machines that constrain the denomination offer — a ready-made replacement/upgrade pipeline. In parallel, ask BNB's Issue Department in writing whether Art.18(1) is treated as a continuing obligation after 01/01/2026; that answer determines whether this is a compliance sell or an efficiency sell.
signals.verifier_note: The DENOMINATION TEXT IS CONFIRMED VERBATIM by independent re-download and pdfminer extraction of the BNB PDF: 2 cassettes = EUR 10 + 20; 3 cassettes = 10 + 20, optionally 5 and/or 50; 4 cassettes = 10 + 20, optionally 5 and/or 50 and/or 100, with (a) sums <=EUR 100 always served from 5/10/20 and/or 50 and (b) sums >EUR 100 may use 50 and/or 100. Art.18(2), Art.19(1)-(2) and Art.20(1)-(5) also confirmed, as are the ZVERB Art.59(1)(4) and Art.59(5)(11) sanction bands. DOWNGRADED TO PARTIALLY-CONFIRMED on one point of characterisation: the researcher called this 'a BINDING ATM DENOMINATION MIX' with no time qualifier. The actual chapeau of Art.18(1) reads 'В срок до датата на въвеждане на еврото' (by the euro introduction date), inside an ordinance whose subject matter is initial frontloading and sub-frontloading. Presenting it as a perpetual standing mandate overstates the source. opp_size reduced L to M accordingly, and the caveat is now in the signal text so it cannot be dropped downstream. is_new=false: ordinance dates from July 2025.

signals.entity: Bulgarian credit institutions — post-changeover reporting to BNB
signals.signal: [STANDING — dated 31/07/2025; Chapter Four in force from 01/01/2026] BNB Ordinance No.47 of 31 July 2025 on the provision of information by credit institutions under ZVERB Art.26 and on the withholding and expert examination of lev banknotes and coins (DV No.68 of 19/08/2025; in force three days after promulgation except Chapter Four, in force from the euro introduction date). Re-extracted from the BNB PDF this run. Art.2(1)-(2): for the FIRST MONTH after euro introduction banks reported WEEKLY, by 12:00 on the first working day of the week following the reporting week, the total value of lev banknotes and coins held, sent electronically through an information system. Art.2(3): a bank must inform BNB IN ADVANCE of the type and amount of any fee introduced under ZVERB Art.26(6). Art.2(4): a bank must inform BNB IN ADVANCE of the date from which it discontinues cash lev-euro exchange under Art.26(9) — i.e. ahead of 01/01/2027. Art.2(5)-(6): the same advance notification applies to a fee on immediate exchange of DAMAGED lev notes after 6 months, and to discontinuing that service after 12 months. Art.2(7): the Deputy Governor heading the Issue Department may require further exchange-related information. Art.3: customer-facing information must be clearly structured, legible in black-and-white, in Bulgarian or an agreed language, accurate and not misleading. Chapter Four: BNB and banks must withhold any lev note/coin suspected counterfeit or altered; a two-copy protocol on the prescribed form (Annex 1) is raised, one copy to the presenter and one accompanying the notes; delivery to BNB's National Analysis Centre (Cash Centre, 10 Mihail Tenev St, Poligona, 1784 Sofia) within 3 WORKING DAYS of withholding, by registered post or courier AT THE PRESENTER'S COST; BNB carries out the authenticity examination within 20 WORKING DAYS OF ARRIVAL and issues a technical expertise protocol; Art.7 — the result is not open to challenge; Art.9(1) — counterfeits are retained, destroyed and not compensated; Art.9(2) — the equivalent of genuine notes is reimbursed IN EURO to the withholding institution, which then informs the presenter; Art.8(3) — the withholding institution must notify the presenter in writing within 3 working days of receiving the protocol. Legal basis: ZVERB Art.26(12) and (14), BNB Governing Council Decision No.382 of 31/07/2025. Related: BNB Ordinance No.48 of 31/07/2025 governs exchange of DAMAGED lev banknotes and coins into euro.
signals.source_name: BNB Ordinance No.47 of 31/07/2025 (PDF, Bulgarian) — re-downloaded independently this run (HTTP 200, 150 KB) and text-extracted with pdfminer
signals.implies: (a) WHO: all Bulgarian banks. (b) WHAT: branch/back-office cash automation and document management to generate the withholding protocols (Annex 1) and the electronic BNB submissions; counterfeit-detection-capable Glory / Sesami TCRs at the counter cut the manual protocol and courier burden, and the courier cost sits with the presenter, which is a live customer-experience argument for detecting at the counter rather than after acceptance; Printec managed services for the reporting pipeline. (c) WHEN: small ticket in itself, but the Art.2(4) advance-notification duty forces every bank to take and formalise its lev-exchange wind-down decision in Q4 2026 — that is the moment to be in the room with the branch cash-automation business case.
signals.followup: Request from BNB's Issue Department (or from clients) the electronic reporting format and the instructions issued under §2 of the transitional provisions — these are not published on the public BNB site. Treat any question about the non-appealable Art.7 finding or reimbursement disputes as a legal matter for Printec Compliance, not for research.
signals.verifier_note: CONFIRMED in full by independent re-download and pdfminer extraction. Art.2(1)-(7) verified word for word, including the 12:00 first-working-day weekly deadline, the advance-notification duties in (3)-(6) and the Deputy Governor power in (7). Chapter Four verified: Art.4(2) two-copy protocol per Annex 1; Art.5(1) 3 working days; Art.5(2) the NCA address at 10 Mihail Tenev St, 1784 Sofia, with postal/courier costs on the presenter; Art.6(1) 20 working days FROM ARRIVAL AT BNB (the researcher wrote 'BNB completes the examination within 20 working days', which is right in substance but the clock starts on receipt, not on withholding); Art.7 non-appealable; Art.9(1) destruction without compensation; Art.9(2) reimbursement in euro. CORRECTED source_date: the researcher had entered 31/12/2026, a future date that is the deadline, not the source date — set to the ordinance date 31/07/2025 (promulgated DV No.68, 19/08/2025), deadline field retains 31/12/2026. Added Art.3 and Art.8(3), and the legal basis (ZVERB Art.26(12) and (14), GC Decision No.382). is_new=false.

signals.entity: ECB and all euro-area national central banks — footprint: Austria, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Greece, Slovakia, Slovenia
signals.signal: On 23/07/2026 the ECB published TEN SHORTLISTED DESIGNS for the NEXT SERIES of euro banknotes, drawn from over 1,200 entries and selected by an independent jury of 21 experts (graphic design through to neuroscience), and opened a PUBLIC SURVEY OPEN UNTIL 21/09/2026 on two themes — 'European culture' and 'Rivers and birds'. A parallel survey of a representative sample of euro-area citizens runs alongside. The ECB states the Governing Council is 'expected to take the final decision on the new banknote design around the end of the year' (end-2026), informed by the jury's conclusions, a technical assessment and the two surveys. CRITICAL FOR PLANNING: the ECB says only that notes of the new series will enter circulation 'in the coming years' and that existing banknotes will REMAIN LEGAL TENDER and circulate alongside the new ones — NO production date, NO issuance date and NO machine re-certification deadline has been published. Do not assume one, and do not let a bid team assume one. Stated design objectives are stronger security features, better accessibility for visually impaired users and improved durability/sustainability — the accessibility objective is the one most likely to touch device UX later.
signals.source_name: ECB press release 'ECB reveals shortlisted designs for new banknotes and launches public survey'
signals.implies: (a) WHO: every ATM, recycler, TCR, sorter and self-service cash operator in the seven euro-area footprint countries (AT, BG, HR, CY, GR, SK, SI) — the same population that had to be re-tested for the Europa series. (b) WHAT: eventually a multi-year, footprint-wide note-recognition template/firmware update and, on older hardware, sensor-module retrofit and re-certification against the ECB tested-machines list, across NCR ATMs and recyclers, Glory / Sesami TCRs and x-core-managed estates, plus a large field-service mobilisation. (c) WHEN: nothing to commit yet and no deadline exists. The immediate action is defensive and costs nothing: make firmware-upgradeability to a future banknote series an explicit contractual requirement in every NCR/Glory bid signed in 2026-2027, so the eventual retrofit is a service revenue line rather than a warranty claim.
signals.likelihood: ECB states the design decision is expected around end-2026; issuance date unstated
signals.followup: Track the ECB Governing Council design decision expected around end-2026, then the production/issuance timetable and any ECB tested-machines re-certification programme; brief NCR Atleos and Glory account teams now so the upgradeability clause is in Q4-2026 bids.
signals.verifier_note: CONFIRMED by re-fetching the ECB press release directly. Date 23/07/2026, the two themes, the 21/09/2026 survey closing date, the parallel representative survey and the quoted 'around the end of the year' Governing Council decision all match. Added three verified facts the researcher omitted: ten shortlisted proposals from 1,200+ entries, a 21-expert jury, and — most important for planning discipline — the ECB's explicit statements that the new notes enter circulation 'in the coming years' and that existing notes remain legal tender alongside them. The researcher's individual motif list (Callas, Beethoven, Marie Curie, Cervantes, Leonardo, von Suttner) was NOT itemised in the press release text I re-read; it is plausible but unverified, so it has been removed rather than repeated as fact. is_new changed to false: the release is dated one day BEFORE the 24/07/2026 baseline, so it is very likely already in the baseline file — if the orchestrator confirms it is absent from the 24/07/2026 findings, flip this back to true.

signals.entity: Czechia, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Sweden — the five EU Member States with a derogation (footprint: CZ, HU, RO)
signals.signal: The ECB and the European Commission published their biennial CONVERGENCE REPORTS on 24/06/2026, assessing Czechia, Hungary, Poland, Romania and Sweden. Bulgaria is NOT assessed — it obtained an ad hoc convergence assessment in 2025 and adopted the euro on 01/01/2026. Headline findings, re-read in the ECB press release: 'none of the currencies of the countries under review is participating in the exchange rate mechanism (ERM II)' — the mechanism a country must sit in for at least two years before euro adoption — so on the fastest conceivable path none of them can adopt the euro before roughly 2029-2030. PRICE STABILITY: reference value 2.7%, set as 1.5pp above the average of the three best performers, Cyprus (0.9%), France (1.2%) and Denmark (1.6%), over the reference period June 2025 - May 2026; inflation was CONSIDERABLY ABOVE the reference value in Romania and above it, to a lesser extent, in Hungary and Poland, while Czechia and Sweden were below it. LONG-TERM INTEREST RATES: reference value 5.1%; Poland 5.4%, Hungary 6.7% and Romania 6.7% all fail, Czechia and Sweden pass. PUBLIC FINANCES: Hungary, Poland and Romania all exceeded the 3%-of-GDP deficit threshold in 2025 and all three are in the Excessive Deficit Procedure — Romania since 2020 with the correction deadline extended to 2030, Hungary and Poland since July 2024 with correction deadlines of 2026 and 2028 respectively. LEGAL CONVERGENCE: 'none of the five countries under review was fully compatible with the requirements for the adoption of the euro' — including Czechia. The next scheduled biennial assessment is 2028 unless a Member State requests an ad hoc report as Bulgaria did.

signals.entity: Hungarian government / Ministry of Finance and MNB; Hungarian banks (OTP, Erste HU, K&H, Raiffeisen HU, MBH)
signals.signal: POLITICAL SIGNAL, PRESS-SOURCED ONLY. Following the Tisza party's April 2026 election win, Finance Minister Andras Karman has committed Hungary to meeting the Maastricht criteria and adopting the EURO BY 2030 — i.e. by the end of the government cycle (index.hu, 22/06/2026: 'A kormany 2030-ig teljesiti a maastrichti kriteriumokat, jon az euro' [The government will meet the Maastricht criteria by 2030, the euro is coming]). The concrete, dated near-term trigger is more specific than previously recorded: on 26/06/2026 Karman said the government will submit the REVISED (supplementary) BUDGET BY THE END OF AUGUST 2026, with the 2027 budget and the credible medium-term fiscal path to follow BY THE END OF OCTOBER 2026 (hvg.hu, 26/06/2026: 'Augusztus vegeig benyujtjuk a felulvizsgalt koltsegvetest' [We will submit the revised budget by the end of August]); PM-designate Peter Magyar has said there will be no austerity for the sake of the euro. The anchor criterion is a general-government deficit below 3% of GDP. Karman has said ERM II entry should not be rushed and should be decided once the fiscal criteria are within reach. HARD CAVEATS: this is a political commitment carried in press only — there is NO government decree, NO MNB decision and NO ERM II application; and it is contradicted on the numbers by the 24/06/2026 Convergence Report, which found Hungary in breach on inflation, long-term rates (6.7% v 5.1%), deficit (EDP since July 2024, correction deadline 2026) and legal convergence, and outside ERM II.

signals.entity: Romanian Presidency / Government and BNR; Romanian banks (BCR, BRD, Banca Transilvania, Raiffeisen RO, UniCredit RO)
signals.signal: NEW SINCE THE 24/07/2026 BASELINE. On 01/08/2026 President Nicusor Dan announced a POLITICAL AGREEMENT / consensus on euro adoption in Romania, stating that the future Government — whatever its political composition — together with the BNR will draw up a 'foaie de parcurs' [roadmap] setting out the steps to euro-area accession over the coming years. NO target date and NO ERM II date were given; press coverage explicitly describes the accession calendar as still unclear. This sits directly against the 24/06/2026 Convergence Report, under which Romania meets ONLY the government-debt criterion, with 12-month average inflation CONSIDERABLY above the 2.7% reference value, a long-term interest rate of 6.7% against a 5.1% reference, failure on exchange-rate stability (not in ERM II), an Excessive Deficit Procedure running since 2020 with a corrective deadline of 2030, and BNR legislation requiring amendment for legal convergence. BNR Governor Mugur Isarescu has publicly said several more years are needed. Romanian press analysis puts an early-2030s changeover as conceivable IF Romania entered ERM II in 2027 — that is an ANALYST ESTIMATE, NOT an official date, and must never be quoted as one.

(c) WHEN: no budget before ERM II entry. Exchange is free of charge, at the fixed conversion rate 1 EUR = 7.53450 HRK, in person at HNB, Nikole Jurisica 17, Zagreb, 08:30-15:30 Monday to Friday. NOTE THE CONTRAST WITH BULGARIA: under ZVERB Art.26(1) BNB exchanges lev BANKNOTES AND COINS indefinitely, so Bulgaria has no coin cut-off equivalent to Croatia's 31/12/2025 — a Bulgarian client cannot be told 'Croatia shows your coins expire', because they do not.

signals.entity: Central Bank of Montenegro (CBCG) and Central Bank of Kosovo (CBK); Montenegrin and Kosovar banks
signals.signal: [STANDING — long-running, with a live accession angle] Montenegro and Kosovo use the euro UNILATERALLY ('euroisation') without being euro-area members. Re-verified on CBCG's own official euroisation page: dual currency with the Deutsche Mark from November 1999; DEM sole legal tender from 1 January 2001; CBCG established 15 March 2001; full conversion to the euro in March 2002. CBCG records that this regime 'differs entirely from the membership in the euro area' and that Montenegro entered it 'before ECOFIN Council adopted the position prohibiting unilateral euroisation'. CBCG expressly states the consequences: NO reference interest rates and no control of the money supply, since it does not issue the euro; NO unconditional lender-of-last-resort capacity, mitigated only by a precautionary backstop allowing withdrawal of UP TO EUR 250 MILLION for systemic liquidity assistance; and negligible seigniorage. Euroisation is handled under Chapter 17 (Economic and Monetary Policy) of Montenegro's EU accession negotiations. The ECB's standing position remains that unilateral euroisation cannot bypass the convergence process. Kosovo's position mirrors Montenegro's. Reports of an accession-treaty formula recognising Montenegro's regime are PRESS-LEVEL and not confirmed in any EU primary document.
signals.source_name: Central Bank of Montenegro (CBCG) — 'Euroisation' official page (core functions / monetary policy); undated standing page, retrieved 02/08/2026
signals.implies: (a) WHO: Montenegrin and Kosovar banks — both markets already run euro cash end to end. (b) WHAT: there is NO changeover project to sell in ME or XK; the euro-adoption product bundle is irrelevant there. What IS relevant is that these estates handle euro banknotes WITHOUT being subject to Eurosystem ECB/2010/14 machine-listing and fitness discipline today. EU accession would import exactly the Ordinance-18-style regime Bulgaria has just adopted — ECB-listed, fitness-capable recyclers, control tests, internal rules and mandatory reporting. That is the credible Printec ask in ME as Chapter 17 advances. (c) WHEN: no committed budget; position now so that recycler/ATM refreshes bought in 2026-27 are already ECB-list compliant and do not have to be replaced post-accession.
signals.likelihood: A compliance mandate is a post-accession event; no dated trigger exists
signals.followup: Track the EU-Montenegro Chapter 17 negotiating position and Commission enlargement-package language on euroisation. Ask CBCG directly whether it intends to align voluntarily with ECB/2010/14 recirculation standards ahead of accession — that would be an early, low-friction recycler mandate and is the single question that would convert this row into a pipeline.
signals.verifier_note: THE CORE IS CONFIRMED by re-fetching the CBCG page: the November 1999 / 1 January 2001 / March 2002 timeline, the CBCG's founding on 15 March 2001, the 'before ECOFIN adopted the position prohibiting unilateral euroisation' wording, and the three stated consequences (no reference rates or money-supply control, constrained lender of last resort, negligible seigniorage). signals.entity: CBBH (Bosnia & Herzegovina), NBS (Serbia), Bank of Albania, NBRNM (North Macedonia), NBU (Ukraine)
signals.signal: [STANDING — context; negative finding] The remaining non-EU footprint markets have NO euro-adoption pipeline and no changeover deadlines. Bosnia & Herzegovina runs a currency board with the convertible mark pegged to the euro at 1.95583 KM/EUR — numerically the SAME rate at which Bulgaria's lev converted, a legacy of both pegs having been set against the Deutsche Mark — so a future BiH changeover would be arithmetically trivial, but it is not on any official timetable and BiH is not an EU member. Serbia, Albania, North Macedonia and Ukraine retain their own currencies (dinar, lek, denar, hryvnia) with no ERM II perspective; the ECB's 24/06/2026 convergence exercise covers only EU Member States with a derogation, so none of these five is even assessed. Their euro-related alignment runs through SEPA accession and payment-system harmonisation, not currency substitution. Written explicitly as context: no primary source states a euro-adoption date for any of these five, and none should be implied.
